why:
`QoSLivelinessPolicy::is_manual()` — `true` for `ManualByNode` and `ManualByTopic`, the two kinds under which the APPLICATION owns the liveliness assertion.

Ours-only because rclrs exposes the policy as an `rmw` enum with no such predicate. An extension of one line, added by the phase-467 RMW gap-closure design study's Row 7 to be the ONE spelling of a test three call sites were about to write out by hand: `Publisher::assert_liveliness` owes a different answer per kind — a backend with no per-topic lease answers `Unsupported` under a manual kind and `Ok(())` under `Automatic` / `None`, because then there was nothing to assert — and two backends had that `matches!` inline while the `nros-rmw-cffi` NULL-slot arm did not have it at all, which is how the split `rmw_vtable.h` has stated since phase 108 came to be implemented nowhere.

`Unknown` is deliberately NOT manual. It is what a `*_get_actual_qos` read-back writes for a policy the backend could not report, and an absence is not a request; reading it as manual would make a backend with no read-back refuse an assertion nobody asked for. Asserted in `nros-rmw`'s own unit tests, all five variants.
